text: Once upon a time, there was a shepherd boy. He was sitting on a hillside, keeping an eye on the village sheep.
He had been there for hours, and the task felt boring. He wanted something fun to do, but he wasn't sure how to pass the time.

choices.text: Decide to bring a small puzzle or fidget toy next time to keep his hands busy while keeping his eyes on the sheep.
Pretend there is an emergency and call for help to see people's reactions.
Let his mind wander and daydream without watching the sheep at all.

text: Pretending there is an emergency could make it harder for others to know when he truly needs help.

text: He tells himself that next time he will bring a toy with him, but after a while he gets bored and decides to shout out, "Wolf! Wolf! The wolf is chasing the sheep!" to get attention.
The villagers, who trusted the boy, immediately rushed up the hill to help.
But when they arrived, there was no wolf. The boy had tricked them. The villagers felt frustrated.
scene7.prompt: What should the shepherd boy do now?

choices.text: Laugh it off and tell the villagers it wasn't a big deal.
Ignore the villagers and go back to watching the sheep.
Apologize and explain it was a joke, promising to be more careful next time.

text: Laughing it off does not acknowledge why the villagers are frustrated.

text: The boy, still feeling a bit bored, wants to have some fun again. The villagers all go back to their houses, and then the boy shouts again, "Wolf! Wolf! The wolf is chasing the sheep!"
The villagers, now upset, come up the hill but find there is no wolf. They warn him sternly that they won't come next time.
Later that day, the boy sees a real wolf near the sheep. The wolf is getting closer, and the boy gets scared. He immediately shouts, "Wolf! Wolf! The wolf is chasing the sheep!"
But this time, the villagers think he's tricking them again. No one comes to help. The boy feels desperate and starts to panic.
